title: Test an environment-dependent branch through a seam, not the real detector
rule: When code takes a different path by what it detects about its environment (a Flatpak or other sandbox, an OS feature, an env var, a marker file), put the detection result behind a parameter (a crate-private fn taking the env lookup and the file check) and unit-test both answers through it. Also test the wiring end to end once: a child process of the test binary with the variable set, asserting the user-visible result (an option hidden, a note shown) and that the child ran exactly one test. A test that compares against the real detector (`assert_eq!(x.is_some(), !sandboxed())`) only ever runs the common path on CI, so deleting the branch keeps it green.
rationale: E17.3 (#128): the Flatpak branch that hides Start at login and adds a Platform note was tested only in parts; CI never runs in a Flatpak, so removing the check or passing false to the notes left every test green.
